objective: Remove anonymous invocation of privileged admin API entry points while preserving member, media, administrator and server-to-server behavior.
productionBaselineEvidence: 2026-11-12 read-only Supabase production audit: main public 542 tables all RLS enabled; 58 admin_* SECURITY DEFINER functions executable by anon and authenticated. Exact grant migration passed BEGIN/ROLLBACK-only SQL check; production grants remain unchanged pending release.
chosenApproach: For 58 existing admin_* SECURITY DEFINER functions which already allow authenticated calls, revoke function EXECUTE from PUBLIC and anon and explicitly allow authenticated and service_role; fail migration if any anon admin privileged RPC remains. Include read-only post-deploy SQL verification.
selectionRationale: Small targeted privilege change at database API boundary avoids video, ads, auth client, data schema, and business logic changes, while preserving authenticated admin routes.
alternativeApproaches: Revoke EXECUTE on every public function: rejected because public onboarding, media and legitimate signed-in RPCs would break.
Rely only on existing in-function System Admin checks: rejected because anonymous callers still reach privileged code and every future edit must remain flawless.
preserveBehaviors: Existing authenticated system-admin role checks and SQL bodies are not changed
Unrelated member RPCs and public access routes unaffected
Video, photo, ads, PTT, Wall, points and cash ledgers untouched
No Android OTA or web client update required for this ACL migration
acceptanceChecks: Rollback-only SQL trial proves anonymous admin definer execution becomes zero
Post-release SQL check returns no anonymous admin definer functions
Authenticated privileges to known admin functions remain enabled
Main security advisor reflects fewer anonymous definer findings
No media, points, profile, payout, or frontend code changed
